record.paper_title: Some open problems in Banach space theory
record.original_question: Do there exist infinite-dimensional Banach spaces X and Y such that every compact linear operator from X to Y is nuclear?

evidence.quote:
(Q.2) Does there exist a air of infinite dimensionsal Banach spaces X and Y so
that ever compact operator from X to Y is nuclear ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A bounded linear operator $T: X \to Y$ between Banach spaces is called nuclear if it admits a representation
$$T(x) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} x_n^*(x)\, y_n, \qquad x \in X,$$
with $x_n^* \in X^*$, $y_n \in Y$, and $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \|x_n^*\|\,\|y_n\| < \infty$. The operator $T$ is called compact if the image of the closed unit ball of $X$ has compact closure in $Y$. Every nuclear operator is compact, but in general the converse fails.

Question: Do there exist infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ such that every compact linear operator $T: X \to Y$ is nuclear?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is settled affirmatively. Grothendieck (1955) conjectured that for any infinite-dimensional Banach spaces $X,Y$ there must exist a bounded operator $X\to Y$ that is not nuclear (and in particular asked the compact-vs-nuclear version). In 1983 G. Pisier constructed an infinite-dimensional Banach space $P$ for which the projective and injective tensor norms coincide on $P\otimes P$, which yields infinite-dimensional Banach spaces such that every compact (indeed every bounded) operator between them is nuclear, disproving Grothendieck's conjecture and answering the question in the affirmative.

status_evidence.title: Nuclear operators between Banach spaces - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In 1983 Gilles Pisier constructed an infinite-dimensional Banach space X such that the projective and injective tensor products X⊗π X and X⊗ε X coincide, disproving Grothendieck's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Pisier's 1983 construction provides infinite-dimensional Banach spaces in which the natural compact/bounded operators are nuclear, settling the question affirmatively.
